record.title: Polynomial realization conjecture for zero Kobayashi–Royden metric in the spectral ball
record.statement:
Let $
obreak\Omega_n$ be the spectral ball of $n\times n$ complex matrices, let $A\in\Omega_n$ and $B\in\mathcal M_n$, and let $
obreak\kappa_{\Omega_n}(A;B)$ denote the Kobayashi–Royden metric at $A$ in the direction $B$. Write $sp(A)$ for the spectrum of $A$.

**Polynomial realization conjecture.** If

$$
\kappa_{\Omega_n}(A;B)=0,
$$

then there is a polynomial mapping $p:\mathbb C\to\Omega_n$ of degree at most $n$ such that

$$
p(0)=A,\qquad p'(0)=B,\qquad sp(p(\lambda))=sp(A)\quad\text{for every }\lambda\in\mathbb C.
$$

The paper proves the conjecture for $n=2$; the general case is left open. The statement strengthens the known existence of an entire mapping with the same initial data and constant spectrum by requiring a polynomial of degree at most $n$.
record.source_name: Nikolai Nikolov, Pascal J. Thomas and Wlodzimierz Zwonek, “Discontinuity of the Lempert function and the Kobayashi–Royden metric of the spectral ball”, arXiv:0704.2470 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.2470

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2007).

record.title: The nucleus characterization conjecture for graph braid groups
record.statement: For a graph $\Gamma$ and a braid index $n\geq 2$, let $B_n\Gamma$ denote its graph braid group. An **$n$-nucleus** is a minimal graph whose $n$-braid group is not a right-angled Artin group, while the $n$-braid group of every graph contained in it is a right-angled Artin group. **Nucleus characterization conjecture.** For every braid index $n\geq 2$, a graph $\Gamma$ contains no $n$-nuclei if and only if $B_n\Gamma$ is a right-angled Artin group. The paper proves this equivalence for $n\geq 5$ and conjectures that it holds for all braid indices.
record.source_name: Jee Hyoun Kim, Ki Hyoung Ko and Hyo Won Park, “Graph braid groups and right-angled Artin groups”, arXiv:0805.0082 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0805.0082

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2008).

record.title: Universal-cycle conjecture for isomorphism classes of graphs
record.statement: Let $k$ be a positive integer. A **U-cycle of isomorphism classes of graphs on $k$ nodes** is a cyclic sequence in which every $k$-window represents a distinct isomorphism class of graphs on $k$ nodes, and every such isomorphism class occurs as a window. **Universal-cycle conjecture.** For each $k \geq 3$, there exists a U-cycle of isomorphism classes of graphs on $k$ nodes. The conjecture proposes a canonical universal-cycle construction for unlabeled graphs; the paper notes that the cases $k=3$ and $k=4$ are possible, while existence for all $k \geq 3$ remains open.
record.source_name: Greg Brockman, Bill Kay and Emma E. Snively, “On Universal Cycles of Labeled Graphs”, arXiv:0808.3610 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.3610

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2008).

record.title: Existence conjecture for k-homogeneous Latin bitrades
record.statement:
Let $k$-homogeneous Latin bitrades be Latin bitrades in which every symbol occurs $k$ times, and let the volume denote the number of entries in the bitrade. **Existence conjecture.** For all $m$ and $k$ with

$$
m \ge k \ge 3,
$$

there exists a $k$-homogeneous Latin bitrade of volume $km$. The preceding results establish this for the ranges treated in the paper, but the assertion is left as a conjecture for all $m$ and $k$ satisfying the stated inequalities.
record.source_name: Behrooz Bagheri Gh. and E. S. Mahmoodian, “On the existence of k-homogeneous Latin bitrades”, arXiv:0810.2214 (2008).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.2214

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2008).

record.title: The regular Ramsey number comparison conjecture
record.statement:
Let $R(k,\ell)$ be the Ramsey number, and let $R^{\mathrm{reg}}(k,\ell)$ denote the corresponding Ramsey number restricted to regular graphs. **Regular Ramsey comparison conjecture.** For every $k\geq 2$ there is a constant $c_k>0$ such that

$$
R^{\mathrm{reg}}(k,\ell)\geq c_k R(k,\ell)
$$

for all $\ell\geq 2$. This conjecture proposes that regularity changes Ramsey numbers by at most a constant factor for each fixed $k$; the source presents it as a plausible natural question, with no resolution indicated.
record.source_name: Noga Alon, Sonny Ben-Shimon and Michael Krivelevich, “A note on regular Ramsey graphs”, arXiv:0812.2386 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.2386

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2008).

record.title: Baker–Rumely lower bound conjecture for the tau constant
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a metrized graph, let $\tau(\Gamma)$ denote its tau constant, and let $\ell(\Gamma)$ denote its total length.

**Baker–Rumely's lower bound conjecture.** There is a universal constant $C>0$ such that, for every metrized graph $\Gamma$,

$$
\tau(\Gamma) \geq C\cdot \ell(\Gamma).
$$

This conjecture asks for a uniform lower bound for the tau constant in terms of the total length. The paper's abstract states that the bound is proved for metrized graphs with edge connectivity at least $5$, while the general conjecture remains unresolved there.
record.source_name: Zubeyir Cinkir, “The tau constant and the edge connectivity of a metrized graph”, arXiv:0901.1481 (2009).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2009). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0901.0407](https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.0407).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.1481

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2009).

record.title: The Sands–Sauer–Woodrow conjecture for 3-coloured tournaments
record.statement: Let $T$ be a finite **3-coloured tournament**, meaning a tournament whose edges are coloured with at most three colours. A tournament is a **$T_3$** if three of its vertices span a non-transitive tournament whose three edges have distinct colours. **Sands–Sauer–Woodrow conjecture.** $T$ has either a triple of vertices that span a $T_3$ or a single vertex that dominates every other vertex monochromatically, meaning that for every other vertex $y$ there is a directed path from the chosen vertex to $y$ all of whose edges have the same colour. This conjecture is the 3-colour case of a problem posed by Sands, Sauer, and Woodrow and attributed by them to Erdős; the supplied text does not establish whether it is open or resolved.
record.source_name: Agelos Georgakopoulos and Philipp Sprüssel, “On 3-coloured tournaments”, arXiv:0904.1967 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0904.1967

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2009).

record.title: Bound on the number of high-degree vertices in crossing-critical graphs
record.statement: A graph is **$k$-crossing-critical** if its crossing number is at least $k$, but every proper subgraph has crossing number smaller than $k$. **High-degree vertex conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$, there exists an integer $D=D(k)$ such that every $k$-crossing-critical graph contains at most $k$ vertices whose degree is larger than $D$. The construction in the source produces linearly many vertices of arbitrarily large degree in relation to $k$, motivating this conjecture as a proposed best-possible bound; its resolution is not given in the source.
record.source_name: Zdenek Dvorak and Bojan Mohar, “Crossing-critical graphs with large maximum degree”, arXiv:0907.1599 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.1599

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2009). “The second conjecture was proposed as an open problem in the 1990's by Carsten Thomassen and formulated as a conjecture by Richter and Salazar.”

record.title: Ideal Waring's conjecture
record.statement:
For each integer $k\ge 2$, let $g(k)$ be the least integer such that every positive integer is a sum of at most $g(k)$ $k$th powers, and define

$$
I(k)=2^k+\left\lfloor(3/2)^k\right\rfloor-2.
$$

**Ideal Waring conjecture.** For every $k\ge 2$,

$$
g(k)=I(k).
$$

This is the conjectural exact form of the lower bound arising from the standard obstruction near $3^k$. The general assertion remains open, although many individual values of $k$ are known.
record.source_name: Michel Waldschmidt, “Perfect Powers: Pillai's works and their developments”, arXiv:0908.4031 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0908.4031

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2009).

record.title: The monochromatic-line conjecture for coloured planar point sets
record.statement: Let $P$ be a finite set of points in the plane, and colour each point with one of $k$ colours. A **monochromatic line** means a maximal set of collinear points in $P$ whose points all receive the same colour. **Monochromatic-line conjecture.** For all positive integers $k$ and $\ell$ there is an integer $n$ such that every set $P$ of at least $n$ points in the plane contains $\ell$ collinear points or a monochromatic line. This is presented as a strengthening of the Big-Line-Big-Chromatic-Number Conjecture; no resolution is given in the source.
record.source_name: Attila Pór and David R. Wood, “On Visibility and Blockers”, arXiv:0912.1150 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0912.1150

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2009). “BigClique} is true for $k\leq 5$ or $\ell\leq3$ , and is open for $k=6$ or $\ell=4$.”

record.title: Kajitani's cyclic arboricity conjecture for matroids
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a finite loopless matroid with ground set $E$ and rank function $r(A)$ for subsets $A\subseteq E$. A **cyclic ordering** of $E$ is an ordering considered cyclically, and a block of $r(M)$ cyclically consecutive elements is a base when it has rank $r(M)$. **Kajitani's conjecture.** There is a cyclic ordering of $E$ such that every $r(M)$ cyclically consecutive elements are bases of $M$ if and only if, for every non-empty subset $A\subseteq E$, 
$$
\frac{|A|}{r(A)}\leq\frac{|E|}{r(M)}.
$$
 This conjecture is a much more general formulation of the preceding cyclic-ordering questions; the source reports no resolution, while noting that the two-base generalisation has no known results for $k\geq3$.
record.source_name: Jan van den Heuvel and Stéphan Thomassé, “Cyclic Orderings and Cyclic Arboricity of Matroids”, arXiv:0912.2929 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0912.2929

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2009).

record.title: The dimension formulas for the codes C(1,q) and C(2,q) over odd prime powers
record.statement:
Let $q$ be an odd prime power, and let $C(1,q)$ and $C(2,q)$ be the codes defined from the incidence structures in the paper. Their dimensions are the integers $\dim C(1,q)$ and $\dim C(2,q)$. **Dimension conjecture.**

$$
\dim C(1,q)=\frac{1}{2}q^3-q^2+\frac{3}{2}q-1,
$$

$$
\dim C(2,q)=\frac{1}{2}q^3-\frac{5}{2}q^2+\frac{9}{2}q-\frac{7}{2}.
$$

These formulas were obtained by interpolation from computed tables and are verified in the source for every odd prime power $q$ with $5\leq q\leq31$; their validity beyond that range is not established.
record.source_name: Alain Couvreur, “Incidence structures from the blown-up plane and LDPC codes”, arXiv:1004.3774 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.3774

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2010).

record.title: Universality conjecture for the word $u_N$ in the 0-Hecke algebra
record.statement:
Let $H_0(S_N)$ be the 0-Hecke algebra of the symmetric group, and let

$$
u_N=(1,2,\ldots,N-2,N-1,N-2,\ldots,2,1).
$$

For a signed diagram $D$ on the letters $1,\ldots,N-1$, let $u_N^D$ be the masked word obtained by applying the sign of each letter in $D$ to its occurrences in $u_N$. A word is **universal** if it contains every letter in $\{1,\ldots,N-1\}$ at least once and its masked word is demipotent for every signed diagram.

**Universality conjecture.** The word $u_N$ is universal.

This conjecture proposes a uniformly describable family of demipotents whose masked versions remain demipotent for every choice of signs. It is based on computer exploration, and the source does not provide a proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Tom Denton, “A Combinatorial Formula for Orthogonal Idempotents in the 0-Hecke Algebra of the Symmetric Group”, arXiv:1008.2401 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.2401

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2010).

record.title: Dejean's conjecture on distant repetitions in c-ary sequences
record.statement: Let $c\geq 5$. An infinite **$c$-ary sequence** is a sequence over an alphabet of $c$ symbols. Two identical blocks of length $n$ are **separated** by the number of terms between the blocks. **Dejean's conjecture.** For every $c\geq 5$, there is an infinite $c$-ary sequence such that, for all $n$, any two identical blocks of length $n$ are separated by at least $(c-2)n$ terms. This conjecture generalizes square-free and related nonrepetitive sequence problems by requiring repeated blocks to be sufficiently far apart; the supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Wesley Pegden, “Highly nonrepetitive sequences: winning strategies from the local lemma”, arXiv:1010.5772 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1010.5772

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2010).

record.title: Coprime-endpoint equality implies canonical offsets
record.statement:
Let $p_i$ be the $i$-th prime, and let $F_k$ be the set of integers divisible by at least one of $p_1,\ldots,p_k$. Let $k\ge3$ and let $l$ be a positive integer. For an integer $a$ satisfying

$$
-p_{k+1}+1\le a\le p_1p_2\cdots p_k-p_{k+1},
$$

and $(a,p_1p_2\cdots p_k)=1$, let $B_{k,l}(a)$ be a subset of $[-p_{k+1}+1,a]$ such that

$$
\{p_1p_2\cdots p_kl+b:b\in B_{k,l}(a)\}
$$

contains no $k+1$ pairwise coprime integers.

**Coprime-endpoint bound conjecture.** For every such $k,l,a$,

$$
|B_{k,l}(a)|\le |F_k\cap[-p_{k+1}+1,a]|.
$$

The coprimality condition on $a$ is an additional restriction in the paper's auxiliary formulation. It is intended to support the eventual form of Erdős's conjecture.
record.source_name: Yong-Gao Chen and Xiao-Feng Zhou, “On Sequences Containing at Most 4 Pairwise Coprime Integers”, arXiv:1101.0050 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.0050

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of January 2011).

record.title: Mader's cubic-order conjecture for 3-critically connected graphs
record.statement:
A graph is **3-critically $k$-connected** if $kappa(G-X)=k-3$ for every $Xsubseteq V(G)$ with $|X|leq3$. Write $|V(G)|$ for the number of vertices of $G$.

**Mader's cubic-order conjecture.** There exists a constant $c>0$ such that every $3$-critically $k$-connected graph has at most

$$
c k^{3/2}
$$

many vertices.

This would bound the order of 3-critically connected graphs in terms of their connectivity and would obstruct certain constructions of large-diameter examples. The source gives no resolution evidence.
record.source_name: Matthias Kriesell, “Minimal Connectivity”, arXiv:1101.2357 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.2357

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2011).

record.title: The universal-word conjecture for demipotents in the 0-Hecke algebra
record.statement:
Let $I$ be the index set, let $D$ be a signed diagram, and let $w^D$ be the masked word obtained by applying the sign of each index in $D$ to every occurrence of that index in $w$. A word is **universal** if it contains every letter in $I$ at least once and $w^D$ is demipotent for every signed diagram $D$. For $N$, define

$$
u_N=(1,2,\ldots,N-2,N-1,N-2,\ldots,2,1).
$$

**Universal-word conjecture.** The word $u_N=(1,2,\ldots,N-2,N-1,N-2,\ldots,2,1)$ is universal.
This conjecture proposes a uniform, simple expression whose signed versions produce demipotents in $H_0(S_N)$. The supplied text gives computer exploration as motivation but does not state a resolution.
record.source_name: Tom Denton, “Excursions into Algebra and Combinatorics at q=0”, arXiv:1108.4379 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1108.4379

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2011).

record.title: Finiteness conjecture for $r$-primitive graphs
record.statement: Let $r\geq 3$. An **$r$-primitive graph** is a uniquely $K_r$-saturated graph with no dominating vertex. **Finiteness conjecture.** For each $r\geq 3$, there are a finite number of $r$-primitive graphs. The major open question is whether the number of $r$-primitive graphs is finite for every fixed $r$; known examples include complements of odd cycles and several sporadic graphs, and regularity is not necessary.
record.source_name: Stephen G. Hartke and Derrick Stolee, “Uniquely K_r-Saturated Graphs”, arXiv:1203.1084 (2012).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2011–2012). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1104.5261](https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.5261).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.1084

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2012). “The major open question in this area concerns the number of $r$-primitive graphs for a fixed $r$.”

record.title: The unfriendly partition conjecture for countable graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a countable graph. An **unfriendly bipartition** of $G$ is a bipartition of $V(G)$ such that every vertex has at least as many neighbours in the other class as in its own.

**Unfriendly partition conjecture.** Every countable graph admits an unfriendly bipartition.

Every finite graph has an unfriendly bipartition, but the corresponding assertion for countably infinite graphs is a major open problem in infinite graph theory.
record.source_name: Jan Ouborny and Max Pitz, “All graphs are majority 3-choosable”, arXiv:2505.06031 (2025).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2009–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0901.4858](https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.4858).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06031

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2025). “The corresponding problem for infinite graphs has become one of the best-known open problems in infinite graph theory.”

record.title: Bounded-degree polynomial growth conjecture for nonnegative Bakry–Émery graphs
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph with degree bound $d_*$, and let $B(x,r)$ denote the open ball of radius $r$ about $x$. Assume the degree and curvature hypotheses referred to as Assumptions~ and~. **Bounded-degree polynomial growth conjecture.** There is a finite exponent $D(d_*)$ such that

$$
\#B(x,r)\leq r^{D(d_*)}
$$

for every $x\in V$ and every integer $r\geq1$. The surrounding discussion presents this as the general bounded-degree case of the classical dimension-free conjecture; the cited edge-regular case is known, while the arbitrary bounded-degree case is described as remaining open.
record.source_name: Qi Guo, Xueping Huang and Yi C. Huang, “Nonnegative Bakry–Émery Curvature on Bounded-Degree Graphs Implies Volume Doubling and Poincaré Inequalities”, arXiv:2607.15522 (2026).
record.references:
**26 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2011–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2607.12461](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12461), [arXiv:2604.16046](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.16046), [arXiv:2509.24609](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.24609), [arXiv:2501.10828](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.10828), [arXiv:2406.09302](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.09302), [arXiv:2402.15834](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.15834), [arXiv:2311.05500](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.05500), [arXiv:2306.14532](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.14532), [arXiv:2305.16258](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16258), [arXiv:2205.09547](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.09547), [arXiv:2108.01162](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.01162), [arXiv:2010.07191](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.07191), and 13 more.
